changelog.change: Added a 'when blood isn't available / austere settings' section — freeze-dried plasma (room-temperature, plasma-only, not a red-cell substitute) and crystalloid choice by population (balanced for sepsis; saline favoured in isolated TBI).
Initial entry — ATLS hemorrhage class table, MTP activation + ratio + adjuncts + targets, permissive hypotension.

summary: Give balanced product early (1:1:1), tranexamic acid within 3 hours of injury, and calcium after every few units — citrate chelates calcium and hypocalcaemia is a killer. Permissive hypotension (SBP 80–90) until surgical control, EXCEPT in TBI where you keep MAP ≥ 80.

body.text: Beta-blockade, youth, and pregnancy blunt the tachycardic response — a 'normal' heart rate does not exclude class III. Base deficit and lactate track the true deficit better than vital signs.
Activate for uncontrolled haemorrhage needing ≥ 3 units of red cells in 1 hour, an anticipated ≥ 10 units in 24 hours, or an ABC score ≥ 2.

rows: 1 g IV over 10 min within 3 h of injury, then 1 g over 8 h (CRASH-2). Do NOT give if > 3 h from injury
Calcium chloride 1 g IV (or calcium gluconate 3 g) after every 4 units of red cells, or for an ionised Ca < 1.1 mmol/L — citrate toxicity
Target > 150–200 mg/dL — cryoprecipitate (10 units) or fibrinogen concentrate if low
Target ≥ 50 ×10⁹/L; ≥ 100 ×10⁹/L with TBI or ongoing bleeding
SBP 80–90 (or a palpable radial pulse / mentating) until surgical control — EXCEPT traumatic brain injury: keep MAP ≥ 80 / SBP ≥ 110
Reverse anticoagulants (PCC for warfarin/DOACs, idarucizumab for dabigatran); keep the patient warm (> 36 °C); correct acidosis — the lethal triad

body.text: Stop the bleeding: direct pressure, wound packing, a windlass tourniquet for a limb, a pelvic binder for an unstable pelvis, and early transfer to the operating room or interventional radiology. Viscoelastic testing (TEG/ROTEM) guides targeted component therapy where available.
When blood isn't available yet — austere / prehospital

items: Freeze-dried (lyophilised) plasma — room-temperature stable, no cold chain or thaw, reconstitutes in ~1 min; supplied as group AB or group A low-titre anti-B so it can be given before the recipient's type is known. First US-licensed product (Ezplaz) July 2026; long-standing NATO/French-military use. It is plasma ONLY — it restores clotting factors and volume but NOT oxygen-carrying capacity, so it complements red cells / whole blood, it does not replace them.

Crystalloid choice is population-specific, not universal: balanced solutions (Hartmann's, Plasma-Lyte) are the sepsis-driven default and reduce mortality vs saline there; in isolated traumatic brain injury, saline (and starch) outperformed balanced fluids and albumin — the opposite direction — so reach for 0.9% saline when TBI dominates. Albumin is specifically avoided in TBI (SAFE).

Whichever fluid: small aliquots titrated to a radial pulse / mentation (or SBP > 90 with TBI), warmed, and only as a bridge to blood products and haemorrhage control — crystalloid-heavy resuscitation drives dilutional coagulopathy, hypothermia and acidosis.

body.text: Whether prehospital plasma of any kind improves survival is genuinely contested (PAMPer positive; COMBAT and RePHILL negative) — the benefit, where real, concentrates in transport times over ~20 minutes. Treat it as reasonable in long-transport / resource-limited settings, not as established for every profile.
